resources.string: Simplified adult anatomy, not to scale. The views show tissue relationships and examples of variation, not measurements or diagnostic criteria. Playback highlights stationary anatomy.
Vulva is the name for the external genital region. In this schematic, the outer folds flank the inner folds, which border the vestibule.
The labia majora are the outer folds. Their skin and underlying fatty tissue provide a layer of covering and cushioning beside the inner folds.
The labia minora sit medial to the outer folds and help protect the vestibule. The vestibule contains the urethral and vaginal openings, omitted in this close-up.
Fold outline and prominence vary among adults. These two fixed profiles are examples of the same arrangement, not standards for comparison.
The vestibule lies between the inner folds and is part of the external vulvar region. It is not the internal vaginal canal. The folds provide covering without forming a sealed barrier.
Lloyd et al.: variation in adult vulvar anatomy
Adult vulva: simplified external boundaries and fold arrangement
Labia majora: transverse schematic of skin and cushioning tissue
Labia minora: magnified view of the folds bordering the vestibule
The outline marks the extent of this regional schematic, not a sharp anatomical border.
The labia majora flank the inner folds and provide an outer layer of covering.
The labia minora lie medial to the outer folds. Their prominence and outline vary.
The area between the inner folds contains the urethral and vaginal openings, which are not drawn here.
The contour shows the skin covering the outer fold in this section.
The fatty tissue beneath the skin contributes to the bulk and cushioning of the outer fold.
In this cross-section, the surface of the vestibule lies between the two inner folds.
The medial edge of the inner fold borders the vestibule. It is shown as a contour, not a closed seal.
